recognize_zh: 油鏡下單一芽細胞，核佔大部分細胞、染色質細緻均勻、核仁淡，只有一圈深藍無顆粒細胞質；箭頭指向細胞表面的小突起（cytoplasmic blebs），形態屬淋巴芽細胞，Ph+ 無法由外觀判定。
features: Single blast about 1.5–2 times RBC diameter with very high N:C ratio
Round nucleus with finely stippled, evenly dispersed chromatin
Thin rim of deeply basophilic agranular cytoplasm
describe_en: High-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows a single blast with a round nucleus occupying most of the cell, finely dispersed chromatin, faint nucleoli, and a thin rim of deeply basophilic agranular cytoplasm. Small cytoplasmic projections or blebs are present at the cell surface (arrow). No granules or Auer rods are seen. The morphology is that of a lymphoblast; cytoplasmic blebs are nonspecific and do not indicate lineage or genotype. Findings are consistent with acute lymphoblastic leukemia, with Philadelphia chromosome status requiring cytogenetic or molecular confirmation.

ddx.vs: Megakaryoblasts characteristically show prominent cytoplasmic blebbing too, but express CD41/CD61 and lack TdT and B-lymphoid markers.
Hairy cells have mature oval nuclei and abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm with circumferential fine projections, not blastic chromatin with scant cytoplasm.
Myeloblasts tend to have more cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli, and may contain azurophilic granules or Auer rods with MPO positivity.
